catCow.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
catCow.description: A gentle flow between two poses that warms up the spine and relieves tension.
instructions: Start on hands and knees in a tabletop position
Inhale: Drop belly, lift head and tailbone (Cow)
Exhale: Round spine, tuck chin to chest (Cat)
proTips: Keep movements slow and controlled
Focus on feeling each vertebra move
Great as a morning wake-up stretch

threadNeedle.name: Thread the Needle
threadNeedle.description: A rotational stretch that opens up the upper back and shoulders.
instructions: Slide right arm under body, palm up
Rest right shoulder and temple on floor
Return and repeat on left side
proTips: Keep hips level and stacked over knees
Use top hand for support or reach overhead
Breathe into the stretch

shoulderSqueeze.name: Shoulder Blade Squeeze
shoulderSqueeze.description: Strengthens the muscles between your shoulder blades to improve posture.
instructions: Sit or stand with arms at sides
proTips: Imagine holding a pencil between shoulder blades
Keep neck relaxed
Do this hourly if you work at a desk

thoracicExtension.name: Thoracic Extension
thoracicExtension.description: Opens up the upper back to counter forward hunching.
instructions: Sit on heels or in a chair
Gently arch upper back, looking up
proTips: Move from the upper back, not lower back
Keep core lightly engaged
Use a foam roller for deeper stretch

wallAngels.name: Wall Angels
wallAngels.description: A posture-correcting exercise that strengthens upper back muscles.
instructions: Stand with back flat against wall
Press lower back, shoulders, and head into wall
Raise arms to goal post position against wall
Slowly slide arms up and down
Keep all contact points touching wall
proTips: If lower back arches, bend knees slightly
Start with small range of motion
This reveals shoulder mobility limitations

childPose.name: Child's Pose
childPose.description: A restful pose that gently stretches the lower back and hips.
instructions: Kneel on floor with toes together
Fold forward, extending arms in front
proTips: Spread knees wider for more hip opening
Use a pillow under forehead if needed
Focus on elongating the spine

kneeToChest.name: Knee to Chest Stretch
kneeToChest.description: Gently stretches the lower back and glutes.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent
Keep other foot flat or extended
proTips: Keep shoulders relaxed on floor
Breathe into the lower back
Try pulling both knees in together

pelvicTilt.name: Pelvic Tilt
pelvicTilt.description: Activates core muscles and gently mobilizes the lower spine.
instructions: Lie on back with knees bent, feet flat
Flatten lower back into floor by tilting pelvis
proTips: Imagine pulling belly button to spine
Keep breathing throughout
Movement should be small and controlled

supineTwist.name: Supine Spinal Twist
supineTwist.description: A relaxing twist that stretches the lower back and improves rotation.
instructions: Lie on back with arms out to sides
Lower both knees to one side
Hold and breathe, then switch sides
proTips: Keep shoulders grounded
Use gravity, don't force the stretch
Great before bed for relaxation

birdDog.name: Bird Dog
birdDog.description: A stability exercise that strengthens the lower back and core.
instructions: Extend right arm forward, left leg back
proTips: Move slowly to challenge balance
Keep core engaged throughout
Imagine balancing a cup on your back

deadBug.name: Dead Bug
deadBug.description: A core stability exercise that protects the lower back.
instructions: Lie on back with arms reaching to ceiling
Lower opposite arm and leg toward floor
Keep lower back pressed to floor
proTips: Move slowly and with control
Exhale as you extend
Stop if lower back arches

plank.name: Forearm Plank
plank.description: The classic core strengthener that builds overall stability.
proTips: Don't let hips sag or pike up
Squeeze glutes for lower back support
Start with shorter holds, build up

gluteBridge.name: Glute Bridge
gluteBridge.description: Strengthens glutes and hamstrings to support the lower back.
instructions: Lie on back with knees bent, feet flat
Press through heels to lift hips
Create straight line from shoulders to knees
proTips: Don't hyperextend the lower back
Drive through heels, not toes
Add a pause at the top for intensity

sidePlank.name: Side Plank
sidePlank.description: Targets the obliques and lateral stabilizers.
instructions: Lie on side with elbow under shoulder
Lift hips to create straight line
proTips: Modify by dropping bottom knee
Keep hips stacked, don't roll forward
Engage core before lifting

crunch.name: Modified Crunch
crunch.description: A controlled crunch that targets the upper abdominals safely.
instructions: Lie on back with knees bent
Place hands behind head for support
Lift shoulders off floor using abs
proTips: Don't pull on your neck
Focus on the squeeze, not the height
Exhale as you lift

tip-1.title: Consistency Over Intensity
tip-1.content: 10 minutes daily beats 1 hour once a week. Small, regular practice builds lasting strength and habits.

tip-2.title: Desk Break Reminder
tip-2.content: Set a timer to stand and stretch every 30-45 minutes. Your spine needs regular movement to stay healthy.

tip-3.title: Breathe Into the Stretch
tip-3.content: Deep breathing helps muscles relax and increases the effectiveness of stretches. Never hold your breath.

tip-4.title: Listen to Your Body
tip-4.content: Sharp pain is a stop sign. Mild discomfort during stretching is normal, but pain is not. Adjust as needed.

tip-5.title: Posture Check
tip-5.content: Ears over shoulders, shoulders over hips. Check your alignment several times throughout the day.

tip-6.title: Sleep Position Matters
tip-6.content: Side sleeping with a pillow between knees reduces spinal stress. Avoid sleeping on your stomach.

tip-7.title: Progress Takes Time
tip-7.content: Spinal flexibility and core strength develop gradually. Celebrate small wins and trust the process.

tip-8.title: Morning Movement
tip-8.content: Your spine is most vulnerable in the morning. Start with gentle movements before intense activity.
